chapters.title: Orchard Core shortcodes
chapters.subtitle: Embed images and links in your text

steps.text: A shortcode is a small tag in square brackets that you type into the text of a page. The site replaces it with a picture or an address. In this video, you insert an image, set its options, and pick shortcodes from a list.

chapters.title: What a shortcode is
chapters.subtitle: A tag that the site replaces

steps.text: Some of what a page shows depends on the site, such as a picture from the media library. You type a shortcode in the text, and the site replaces it with the result when it displays the page. The editor keeps the shortcode itself.

A shortcode starts with a name in square brackets. Options can follow the name, and some shortcodes take content between an opening tag and a closing tag. For an image, that content is the name of a file.

With the Shortcodes feature enabled, the Media module adds the image shortcode, which shows a picture, and the asset_url shortcode, which gives the address of a file. The locale shortcode shows its content for a matching language, and needs the Localization module.

chapters.title: Insert an image
chapters.subtitle: Pick a file from the media library

steps.text: The Article list shows each article with an Edit button. Let's open one. Its body is a text editor, and the toolbar has buttons named Insert Shortcode and Insert Media.
Let's add a picture after the line that introduces the photo. Insert Media opens the media library in a dialog, with its files listed. Each file you select adds its own shortcode.
We select home-bg.jpg and confirm. The dialog closes, and the text holds the image shortcode: the name in square brackets, the file name, and a closing tag.
Publish saves the change. On the published page, the site has replaced the shortcode with the picture from the media library.

Options go after the name. The image shortcode takes alt, for alternative text, and class, for a style class. Width and height ask for a resized copy in the sizes the site accepts, and mode, format and quality shape that copy.
Let's ask for a copy that is 480 pixels wide. Inside the opening tag, after the name, we type the width option with the value 480.
Next comes the alt option. Its text describes the picture for visitors who can't see it, so we type a short description.
After publishing, the page shows a smaller picture. The site served a copy resized to the width we asked for.

chapters.title: Choose a shortcode from a list
chapters.subtitle: Available shortcodes and asset_url

steps.text: Insert Shortcode opens Available Shortcodes. Each shortcode is a card, with a hint and a note on how to write it. The categories on the left narrow the list.
The Filter box matches the start of a name, so typing asset leaves the asset_url card. Add puts that shortcode into the text.
Its two tags have a space between them. We replace the space with the file name post-bg.jpg, so the shortcode points at a file in the media library.
The asset_url shortcode gives only an address, with no picture. After publishing, the page shows the address of the file on the site.

Shortcodes work in the HTML body and the Markdown body of a content item, and in HTML fields and Markdown fields. The Markdown editor with a toolbar has buttons named Insert Shortcode and Insert Image.
You can also type a shortcode by hand, since the buttons only save typing. In the editor, a shortcode stays plain text, and the displayed page shows the result.
Shortcodes let your text carry a picture or an address that the site fills in. Thanks for watching.
